prisoner.name: Peter Sprunger-Froese
prisoner.description: Peter Sprunger-Froese cut the outer fence and entered the Rocky Flats nuclear weapons plant grounds to pray on December 25, 1981. Arrested and taken to jail, the five protesters refused bond at their December 28 arraignment. A January 17, 1982 contemporary report confirms that they remained jailed after a January 8 hearing, facing contempt proceedings for violating an injunction against trespass at the plant.
prisoner.body: Source: National No-Nukes Prison Support Collective newsletter, January 17, 1982, page 1. Custody is historical; an exact release date has not been verified.

case.charges: Contempt of court for violating an injunction against trespass at Rocky Flats.
case.sentence: Pretrial detention: jailed from December 25, 1981 and remanded again January 8, 1982 after declining bond. March 1 trial scheduled. Final disposition and release date not established by this issue.

prisoner.name: Tina Lowe
prisoner.description: Tina Lowe was imprisoned for an October 1979 trespass protest at the Trident submarine base at Bangor, Washington. A January 17, 1982 contemporary prisoner-support newsletter lists her at the federal correctional institution in Pleasanton, California, and reports a six-month sentence imposed November 16, 1981 after she refused to promise not to trespass at the base again.
prisoner.body: Source: National No-Nukes Prison Support Collective newsletter, January 17, 1982, page 2. Custody is historical; an exact release date has not been verified.

case.charges: Trespass at the Trident submarine base, Bangor, Washington.
case.sentence: Six months, imposed November 16, 1981; documented in custody at FCI Pleasanton in the January 17, 1982 report. Exact admission and release dates unverified.

prisoner.name: Ann Clune
prisoner.description: Ann Clune participated in a December 28, 1981 antiwar action at the Pentagon, pouring blood on the River Entrance steps during a Feast of the Innocents witness. A January 17, 1982 contemporary newsletter reports a January 15 trial, a 30 days sentence, and actual confinement at the D.C. Detention Center.

prisoner.name: Tom Joyce
prisoner.description: Tom Joyce, identified as a Toronto peace activist, was arrested during a December 30, 1981 antiwar blood-pouring action at the Pentagon. He refused release on personal recognizance and remained in the D.C. jail. A January 17, 1982 prisoner-support report confirms continued custody after a January 8 court appearance.

case.sentence: Held after refusing personal-recognizance release; continued confinement after January 8, 1982 documented. The reported one-year maximum is not an imposed sentence. Actual release date unverified.
